detected_by: coordinator during requested daily-run health check
system: t5-pipeline daily automation (com.t5pipeline.daily) on Mac mini 100.83.28.83
what_happened: The 2026-08-28 daily run started on schedule at 17:00:01 and completed steps discover, check, lab, execute, analyse successfully. It entered the 'shareholders' step at 17:00:29, fetching 944 companies in 95 batches with a 120s inter-batch delay. The last log line is 'Rate-limit pause: 120s before batch 7/95' at 17:11:11. Nothing follows — no traceback, no 'Daily run SUCCESS', no 'Daily run FAIL', no step completion. The process is not running now and left no exit record.

evidence.t5_pipeline_log_agrees: logs/t5_pipeline.log ends at same timestamp mid-batch (AUTO: no changes) then rate-limit pause
evidence.no_jetsam: log show for jetsam/memorystatus in 17:05-17:20 window returned nothing
evidence.no_crash_report: ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports has no entry for python/t5_pipeline on 2026-08-28
evidence.launchctl_state: state = not running, runs = 0, last exit code = (never exited)

root_cause: UNDETERMINED. The process vanished without writing an exception or exit status. Ruled out by evidence: OOM/jetsam kill (no memorystatus log entries), Python exception (would have written traceback to daily.log which is both StandardOutPath and StandardErrorPath), and normal completion (no terminal SUCCESS/FAIL line). Remaining candidates not yet distinguished: (a) launchd terminated the job, (b) system sleep/power event interrupted the long-running job, (c) external SIGKILL. Note the run was unusually long-lived by design — 944 companies x 120s delay across 95 batches is roughly 3.2 hours of wall clock, versus the 136s the 2026-08-27 run took when 944 companies were freshness-skipped. The Aug 28 run was the first daily to attempt a near-full shareholder scan, so the failure correlates with unprecedented job duration.
contributing_factor: The daily job has no watchdog, no ExitTimeOut, no AbandonProcessGroup handling, and no completion assertion. A silent death is indistinguishable from a job that never ran, so nothing alerted for 3 days.
impact: One daily cycle (data date 2026-08-27) produced no dashboard refresh; output/dashboard.json, ownership.json, transactions.csv are stale as of 2026-08-27 17:01. Shareholder data was independently recovered by the weekly full scan on 2026-08-30 09:23 (962/962 OK, 4 changes, 3 SELL signals on HKMU written to lab.json), so no shareholder signal was permanently lost. No trades affected — executor reported 0 opened / 0 closed / 61 open trades.

secondary_finding.issue: analyse step degraded on every run
secondary_finding.detail: t5_pipeline.analyst logs 'Bonsai unreachable: [Errno 61] Connection refused' on every daily run; step is marked ok with result 'bonsai unavailable'. Confirmed no listener on the Bonsai port — lsof shows only 5000 (ControlCenter), 8000 (dashboard), 8765 (dqf), 8971 (mesh-hub). analyst.py references model path /Users/ptpakdefarma/models/ternary-bonsai-27b. The ternary-bonsai-27b server is not running; com.bonsai.gateway is loaded but the backing model server is absent.
secondary_finding.severity: low — step degrades gracefully, does not fail the run

corrective_action_proposed: Add a completion sentinel: have the daily run write a heartbeat/last-success timestamp file, and alert if it goes stale beyond one scheduled cycle.

Reduce shareholders-step exposure in the daily path — the 120s x 95-batch full scan belongs in the weekly job (which already does it successfully); the daily should cap batches or skip when the freshness-skip count is low.
Investigate whether the Mac mini sleeps or whether launchd reaps long-running jobs; if sleep is the cause, set an appropriate power assertion or move the job to a windowed schedule.
